subject: Service degradation: throughput & latency impact — proposed compensation and next steps
messages:
From: Nathan Brooks <nathan@trellis.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: support@trellis.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + elevated 5xx rate (prod)

Soojin —

We observed a sustained throughput drop and elevated error rates across our production traffic to Redwood between 2026-07-12 02:05 UTC and 2026-07-12 05:40 UTC. Latency spiked from our normal 120ms p50 to ~950ms p50 and 5xxs increased to ~3.8% of requests. This affected our checkout and recommendation flows for ~2.5 hours and caused several customer complaints.

Can you confirm you're tracking this and share a timeline + root cause? Trellis is a paying Dedicated customer; we need to understand impact and next steps for credits/compensation — our finance team is asking for a formal calculation and a statement for our audit.

Attaching our sample logs and a short incident packet.

—Nathan
Nathan Brooks
CEO, Trellis.ai
Nathan@trellis.ai

Attachment: trellis_sample_spans_0712.json (referenced)

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Sudden throughput drop + elevated 5xx rate (prod)

Folks — forwarding Trellis incident. High-severity: Dedicated pool experienced capacity contention followed by degraded latency and an error spike. Nathan is asking for root cause + a compensation calculation they can present to finance.

Summary from ops (internal):
- Impact window: 2026-07-12 02:05 — 2026-07-12 05:40 UTC
- Symptoms: p50 latency up to ~950ms, 5xx ~3.8%, sustained RPS drop ~40% for their critical route
- Preliminary cause: an autoscale fallback on one rack during a kernel upgrade job that increased context-switching; KV-cache priming regressed for warm clients

Ask: rishi — can you run the SLA credit calc (per contract SLAs) and provide a recommended commercial adjustment?
Sean — we should prepare a concise incident timeline for Nathan; cc'ing Evelyn for exec alignment if we need to offer an exception or one-time concession.

I'll coordinate comms with Trellis.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0184

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Fwd: Sudden throughput drop + elevated 5xx rate (prod)

All — attached is a preliminary SLA credit calculation (SLA_credit_calc_v1.xlsx) and a short note on assumptions. Key points:
- Contracted SLA: 99.9% availability per month for the Dedicated cluster (per RW-Dedicated Schedule).
- Incident window produced an availability impact equivalent to 0.12% of monthly uptime for Trellis' cluster (using their observed traffic weight).
- Estimated base credit per SLA: monthly usage * 0.12% * 1.0 (credit multiplier per contract) -> shows as $8,400 on their July bill.
- Recommended commercial offer: standard SLA credit + one-time service credit of $12,000 given customer impact to revenue and to preserve the relationship (total $20,400). Alternatively, offer standard credit + free +1 burst week on Dedicated pool (valued ~ $10k) if they prefer capacity instead of cash.

Notes/risks:
- Legal has to sign off on any deviation from standard terms; finance needs final numbers to cut a credit.
- If we precede with a goodwill credit bigger than the SLA, flag it as \"commercial concession\" and coordinate with revenue ops.

Sean — can you draft the incident timeline doc (short) and a plain-language explanation of cause + mitigation? I'll prepare the spreadsheet and a one-paragraph proposed offer for Nathan.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan@trellis.ai>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 12:11:00 -0400
Subject: Timeline & root cause (Trellis incident 2026-07-12)

Nathan —

Thanks for flagging this. We took ownership immediately when you reached out. Below is a concise timeline and the remediation actions: 

- 2026-07-12 02:04 UTC — Kernel patch roll initiated on one rack in their Dedicated pod (scheduled internal maintenance).
- 02:05 — 02:20 UTC — Autoscaler observed higher load on remaining racks; one worker group experienced elevated context-switches causing degraded performance for some long-lived connections.
- 02:20 — 03:15 UTC — KV-cache priming regressed for warmed clients, causing higher tail latency on critical routes; error rate climbed as retries overlapped.
- 03:15 UTC — Ops detected the abnormal error spike and initiated rollback of the kernel patch and drained affected worker nodes.
- 03:40 — 05:40 UTC — Traffic progressively recovered; by 05:40 UTC we were back to baseline.

Mitigations completed:
- Reverted kernel change on affected rack and set maintenance safeguards to block autoscaler triggers during kernel ops.
- Forced KV-cache rewarm for Trellis's critical route and added proactive priming ahead of maintenance windows.
- Added a short-term increase in capacity for Trellis's Dedicated pool during their business hours next week at no charge (if they prefer).

We own this; I apologize for the disruption. Rishi is proposing an SLA credit calculation and a suggested additional commercial concession. If you'd like, Soojin can set up a short exec-to-exec call with Evelyn for alignment on the commercial resolution.

Best —
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering (Redwood Inference)
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachment: incident_timeline_20260712-0713.pdf

From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan@trellis.ai>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 17:08:00 -0400
Subject: Exec alignment: Trellis incident — proposed customer resolution

Nathan —

I'm Evelyn Hart, VP of Customer Success at Redwood. First, thank you for raising this and apologies for the impact. We appreciate Trellis as a strategic Dedicated customer and want to make this right.

Proposed resolution (we can make this official in a short email or a DocuSign addendum):
1) Standard SLA credit of $8,400 applied to the July invoice (per the attached calc).
2) One-time commercial concession: $12,000 credit OR a complimentary one-week Dedicated burst (your choice).
3) Operational commitments: we will perform a post-mortem report (public redacted version) and schedule a joint runbook review within 10 business days.
4) Two-week elevated SRE support window (dedicated on-call channel + weekly check-ins) at no additional charge.

If that package works, Soojin will send an email to confirm and we will route the credit through finance. If you prefer a different split between cash and capacity, we're open to adjusting.

Again, sincerely sorry for the disruption. We're focused on restoring confidence and preventing recurrence.

Warm regards —
Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Attachment: SLA_credit_calc_v1.xlsx

Nathan replied to Soojin (external): \"Appreciate the fast response and the proposed package. We'll review internally and confirm whether we want cash or capacity. Our finance team will expect the formal calculation. Please send the redacted post-mortem when ready.\"
